title: prepublish.mjs cannot spawn npm on Windows since the Bun 1.4.2 pin, so the tag-time qualification emits no receipt
description:
Found at tag time on the 0.12.0 release, and it is publication-blocking: no native-execution receipt is emitted, so nothing can be staged.

MEASURED: qualification run 36694113900 on the v0.12.0 tag. source-gates success; darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64 success; win32-x64 FAILURE; win32-arm64 FAILURE; candidate-bundle and native-execution-receipt both skipped. Both Windows legs fail at step 7, bun scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs, with package_contents_and_provenance passed, then root_pack FAILED and candidate_smoke_validation FAILED, both reporting "spawn npm.cmd EINVAL" and publicationBlocking: true. root_pack is the first gate that spawns npm, so every npm call in that script is dead on Windows.

ROOT CAUSE, isolated by elimination rather than assumed. prepublish.mjs maps npm to npm.cmd on win32 and handed it to execFile with no shell. A .cmd passed to spawn without a shell now fails EINVAL -- the hardening that followed CVE-2024-27980, which Bun aligned with in the 1.4.x line. What makes the attribution clean instead of a guess: the script, the gate list, the npm.cmd mapping and the Windows runner images (windows-2022, windows-11-arm) are all byte-identical to the v0.11.0 tag, whose qualification run 36285769701 completed SUCCESS on 2026-09-27. The only variable that differs between the two runs is the workflow bun-version: 1.3.14 then, 1.4.2 now.

So the pin move to Bun 1.4.2 (QCLI-411) is what surfaced this. The pin move is not itself wrong; a latent Windows bug in a qualification script was hiding behind the older runtime.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: adding the shell option is the unsafe shape (Node DEP0190 -- arguments are concatenated, not escaped) and it also breaks on any path containing a space, which is exactly the Windows temp path shape this script builds. The fix quotes every argument itself and hands a finished command line to cmd.exe with windowsVerbatimArguments, which is the pattern cross-spawn uses.

VERIFICATION CONSTRAINT, recorded because it shapes the fix: this host is darwin, so the Windows branch cannot be executed here. The helper is therefore a side-effect-free module taking the platform as a parameter, so the win32 argv shape is asserted from any host, and the real proof is the Windows legs of a dispatched matrix run.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The Windows legs of a six-platform dispatch run go green, named by run id and head SHA, with every leg reported individually
The POSIX legs of that same run stay green, so the fix did not regress the path that already worked
prepublish.mjs reaches npm on Windows without EINVAL, and does so without the shell option, which a test refuses by name
The win32 argument shape is asserted from a non-Windows host, so the fix is verifiable without a Windows runner
A path containing a space survives as one argument, which is the specific way the shell-option form fails

implementationNotes:
CORRECTION to this record own ROOT CAUSE paragraph, from the independent review of PR 452 (2026-09-30), re-measured here rather than taken on the report.

The paragraph says the script, the gate list, the npm.cmd mapping and the Windows runner images are "all byte-identical to the v0.11.0 tag", and uses that as the proof that the Bun pin is the only differing variable. That sentence is FALSE as written. `git diff v0.11.0 v0.12.0 -- scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs` is +12/-0, and it carries: a REGISTRY_PINS import, a new breaking_bump gate inside runSourceGates, a comment block, and `...REGISTRY_PINS` added to candidate_clean_install arguments.

What IS unchanged, and what the conclusion actually rests on: the npm spawn MECHANISM (the same execFile call and the same npm -> npm.cmd mapping), the args of root_pack -- the gate that failed -- and the Windows runner images. The EINVAL is raised at spawn time, before any argument is examined, so the added pins could not have caused it. Recorded precisely rather than smoothed over: one npm call did change its arguments; the spawn path and the failing gate did not.

So the conclusion survives and the sentence did not. Corrected wording: the npm spawn path and the Windows runner images are unchanged since v0.11.0; the only workflow variable is the Bun pin; and the current script was never run on 1.3.14 -- what passed there was the v0.11.0 script.

The same over-claim was repeated in the source comment, the test docstring, the PR body and two cross-session reports. Each is corrected at its own site; this record is annotated rather than rewritten, following this repository practice of leaving records as written and labelling them. The failure mode is worth naming: I verified three specific lines and the runner images, then wrote a sentence whose subject was the whole file.

CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY, named by lore-cli 2026-09-30 and recorded here so it is not invisible from this side.

Quest win32-x64 qualification leg being GREEN under the pinned Bun 1.4.2 is load-bearing evidence OUTSIDE this repository. lore-cli has a deterministic win32-x64 failure of its own -- a normal JS rejection at a native driver load (@ladybugdb/core), with bun 1.3.14 -> 1.4.2 the only moved variable on their side -- and opum-cli-e2e offered the same shape as counter-evidence: a runtime transition alone is not sufficient, because quest runs 1.4.2 on a Windows runner and its win32-x64 evidence is green. So this leg is what rules out the runtime transition alone as the cause of THEIR failure, and it points their diagnosis at a bun-1.4.2 x Ladybug interaction instead.

CONSEQUENCE, stated so a later reader does not have to reconstruct it: if this leg is ever re-qualified with caveats, downgraded, found to pass vacuously, or superseded by different evidence, lore-cli conclusion changes with it. Anything that touches the standing of quest win32-x64 under 1.4.2 should be reported to them, not just recorded here.

Measured, so the claim is bounded: quest win32-x64 is NOT a vacuous pass. That leg runs prepublish.mjs end to end -- npm pack, a clean install of the packed tarballs, and candidate_smoke_validation, which EXECUTES the compiled win32 binary (migration-smoke and the manifest/task/projection smokes). A green win32-x64 here means a compiled Windows binary ran and answered, which is a genuinely different object from a leg that never loads the thing under test. The vacuously-passing leg in this area is the one that never touches the native boundary; on lore-cli side that is their win32-arm64 (no Windows-ARM64 addon published, so the driver is never loaded), and they named that themselves.

Also recorded here for the same reason: this record own byte-identical over-claim was corrected in an earlier note, and the corrected version is "the npm spawn mechanism, root_pack arguments and the Windows runner images are unchanged since v0.11.0".

This note asserts nothing about lore-cli root cause and does not claim their failure resembles this one; the mechanisms are different (spawn-level refusal here, in-process addon load there), which was reported to them directly.

CLOSE-OUT VERIFICATION, 2026-09-30 (session 8e31abf1, opum-workflow 0.11.5). All five criteria re-read against live evidence rather than the handoff summary, with two mutations so the assertions are shown to bite. Verdict: five of five, none left open.

AC1/AC2 -- three dispatch runs, every leg individually reported. 36696889019 @ 0f7a7590 (branch fix/QCLI-426-windows-npm-cmd-spawn) and 36699172692 @ 9478e8dd (main, the merged fix): win32-x64, win32-arm64, darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, source-gates and candidate-bundle all success, every POSIX leg green. The tag run 36701023652 @ 9478e8dd (ref v0.12.0) adds native-execution-receipt success and is the receipt the publisher used.

RUN-ID CORRECTION. The 0.11.5-relaunch handoff note on QCLI-421 names the second run as 36799172692; that id returns 404 and denotes nothing. The run it means is 36699172692, same facts, same SHA. Recorded because that note is the pointer the next reader follows.

AC3 -- win32-x64 and win32-arm64 logs of 36701023652: step 7 (prepublish.mjs) success; the gate report shows package_contents_and_provenance, root_pack, platform_pack, immutable_candidate_checksums, candidate_clean_install, candidate_version, candidate_manifest, candidate_task_create, candidate_task, candidate_projection and candidate_migration all passed, with root_pack's executed command visible as cmd.exe /d /s /c with the ABSOLUTE npm.cmd path. EINVAL count is 0 across the 350-line log, whose content is positively confirmed. candidate_smoke_validation records only on the failure branch (prepublish.mjs:310), so its absence from a green report is by construction. Shell-refusal test: adding shell: true to spawn-target.mjs reddened exactly that test with 8 of 9 green, so it refuses the option by name and nothing else.

AC4 -- the full suite ran on this darwin host under the pinned bun 1.4.2: 9 pass, 0 fail. The win32 argv shape is asserted through the platform parameter and an injected env, which is what makes it checkable off Windows. The recorded LIMIT stands and is unchanged: the afterStrip helper encodes the same cmd /s reading the implementation assumes, checked against the Microsoft cmd reference rather than against the implementation.

AC5 -- replacing the per-argument quoting with a plain space join (the DEP0190 shape the shell option would produce) reddened exactly the predicted five tests, the space-argument test among them; the other four stayed green. File restored after, suite re-ran 9 of 9 green, tree clean.

CROSS-REPO STANDING, re-confirmed rather than changed: quest win32-x64 under the pinned Bun 1.4.2 is green and non-vacuous -- the smoke gates execute the compiled Windows binary (task create/list, sqlite and migration smokes). Nothing in this verification weakens the counter-evidence lore-cli uses against a runtime transition alone; the only correction is the run id above, which names the same run.
finalSummary: Fixed the publication blocker: prepublish.mjs now reaches npm on Windows. scripts/qualification/spawn-target.mjs resolves npm to its absolute npm.cmd path and hands cmd.exe a fully quoted command line with windowsVerbatimArguments, replacing the execFile call with no shell that Bun 1.4.2 refuses (EINVAL, the CVE-2024-27980 hardening); the unsafe shell-option form is refused by name in test. Verified by three six-platform dispatch runs -- 36696889019 @ 0f7a7590, 36699172692 @ 9478e8dd, and the receipt run 36701023652 @ 9478e8dd on ref v0.12.0 -- every leg individually green with native-execution-receipt success on the tag run; by the Windows logs showing root_pack passed under cmd.exe with zero EINVAL; by the suite on this host (9/9, pinned bun 1.4.2); and by two mutations showing the space-argument and shell-refusal assertions bite exactly as predicted. Landed as opum-ai/quest-cli#452; dev carries the same bytes as main for all fix files.
